facts.statement: Sierraceratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period found in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Sierraceratops (meaning "Sierra horned face") is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian from the Late Cretaceous Hall Lake Formation of New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in 1997 by geologist Gregory H. Mack on the Armendaris ranch in Sierra County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: In 1997, geologist Gregory H. Mack discovered fossils of a large horned dinosaur on the Armendaris ranch of Ted Turner, founder of CNN, near Truth or Consequences in Sierra County, New Mexico.

facts.statement: The species was formally named and described in 2021 by Dalman, Lucas, Jasinski, and Longrich, with the publication appearing in 2022.
facts.quote: In 2021, the type species Sierraceratops turneri was named and described by Sebastian G. Dalman, Spencer G. Lucas, Steven E. Jasinski, and Nicholas R. Longrich; the final article version was published in 2022.

facts.statement: Sierraceratops was a medium-sized horned dinosaur.
facts.quote: Sierraceratops was a medium-sized horned dinosaur.

facts.statement: Its skull frill was relatively long with large holes separated by an oval-shaped midline bar.
facts.quote: The frill was relatively long and had large holes, the parietal fenestrae, separated by an oval-shaped midline bar.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was originally classified under the genus Torosaurus before being reclassified.
facts.quote: Sierraceratops was originally referred to the genus Torosaurus, based in part on the assumption that the fossils dated to the Late Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Sierraceratops as a sister species to Bravoceratops and Coahuilaceratops, forming a group endemic to the southwestern United States and Mexico.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis by Dalman et al. (2022) recovered Sierraceratops as a sister species to Bravoceratops and Coahuilaceratops, part of a group endemic to the southwestern United States and Mexico.

facts.statement: Sierraceratops belongs to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
The animal is classified within the family Ceratopsidae.
Sierraceratops lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian epochs.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Sierraceratops and Torosaurus are the same animal, but closer study reveals distinct differences in their skull bars.
facts.quote: Closer study later revealed that the animal was distinct from Torosaurus; Torosaurus has a flat midline bar of the parietal, while that of Sierraceratops is oval.

rejected.statement: The only known species, Sierraceratops turneri, is known from a partial skeleton discovered in 1997.
rejected.quote: The genus contains a single species, Sierraceratops turneri, known from a partial skeleton discovered in 1997.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'known from a partial skeleton discovered in 1997'

rejected.statement: The holotype fossil dates to approximately 72 million years ago during the Campanian-Maastrichtian stages.
rejected.quote: The holotype, NMMNH P-76870, was found in a layer of the Hall Lake Formation, dating from the Campanian-Maastrichtian, about seventy-two million years old.

rejected.statement: Unlike other chasmosaurs, it possessed short but massive brow horns and a long cheek horn on the jugal bone.
rejected.quote: Compared to other chasmosaurs, it has short but massive brow horns that are relatively short and robust and a long cheek horn on the jugal.
